LG G4 supplied by LG for my company, unlimited talk and text within my country and 2GB data.

A quick review:

I love stock Android, especially the Nexus line for the rapid updates. Because of that, my biggest disappointment with the G4 is the native stock options. Double tap to turn the screen on/off is probably the coolest feature of the phone, but I hate the stock LG launcher (Nova is my go-to), which makes it tough to use without root. If I actually owned this phone, it would be perfect because I could root to fix that one little gripe I have.

I'm really looking forward to the G5 (Which I might actually buy instead of asking LG for a demo) due to them fixing the only other major issue I have: no fingerprint scanner.

The speed right out of the box is great, even with the Snapdragon 805, however when I encrypted the device, there was a distinct drop in speed. I find the device does still heat up in graphic-intensive games or higher powered emulators (Drastic, I'm looking at you!).

The camera is probably the best I have seen on a smartphone in recent years. It does lack the post-processing polish of say an S6 or an iPhone 6s, but if you spend a couple seconds in Snapseed, you can come up with some amazing photos.

All-in-all I'd give the G4 a solid 9/10 for the awesome camera, the speed, removable storage and battery and double tap on/off. It loses a point for non-stock (aka slow update times), no fingerprint scanner and requiring root for OCD obsessed power users like me.

TLDR;

  • Fast, but slower when encrypted
  • No Stock
  • The camera is awesome.
  • Removable battery and Storage
  • No fingerprint scanner is a big let-down.
  • Double Tap on/off is really cool, but only works with the stock launcher.
